text:
maria: Heads-up: several GPU nodes in us-west2 are showing NotReady + NoSchedule and GPU pods are stuck pending. Noticed this ~12m ago after the nodepool kernel patch window. anyone else seeing this? :frowning:
kenji: I see the alert. Can you paste `kubectl get nodes | grep gpu` and `kubectl describe node <node>` for one of the affected nodes?
maria: pasted outputs below:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu
gpu-pool-7x9k   NotReady   <none>   70d   192.168.12.45   us-west2-a
gpu-pool-8y2m   NotReady   <none>   3d    192.168.12.61   us-west2-b
```
`kubectl describe node gpu-pool-7x9k` shows kubelet not ready and taint `node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute` and `nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule`
Logs from kubelet look like device plugin failing to register.
```
Jun 22 10:42:11 gpu-pool-7x9k kubelet[2345]: E06022 10:42:11.123] Device plugin registration failed: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to list devices: open /var/lib/nvidia: no such file or directory
```
raj: that's the device-plugin crashloop I've seen before when driver modules didn't load after kernel patch. `nvidia-smi` on the node returns `command not found` or kernel oops?
sophia: @maria can you `kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset -p` for the node to confirm? infra-oncall-bot is also spamming alerts.
maria: logs from the daemonset (recent crashloop) below:
```
I0622 10:40:02.345] Starting nvidia device plugin v0.11
E0622 10:40:05.678] failed to discover GPUs: failed to run nvidia-smi: exit status 127
```
k8s-deploy-bot: recent rollout: `daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset` was rolled 11m ago (image: nvidia/k8s-device-plugin:v0.11.0) by infra/driver-automation
kenji: that exit 127 means the nvidia CLI/tools aren't present — likely kernel module didn't survive the kernel update. We should check `systemctl status nvidia-persistenced` and `lsmod | grep nvidia` on the host.
maria: checked: `systemctl status nvidia-persistenced` shows failed, `lsmod` empty for nvidia. dmesg shows `nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout` errors.
raj: yep that's a kernel-module ABI mismatch. The system kernel was bumped and the driver installed previously is incompatible. The node is unusable until we rebuild/reinstall the driver matching the kernel or roll forward to a compatible driver.
sophia: cluster-autoscaler note: CA has not scaled up additional GPU nodes because the NodeGroup is at its max size (quota). We currently have a soft max set for gpu-pool. If we bring these nodes back, we still need capacity headroom for pending jobs.
cloudops: cc @sophia we can temporarily increase the nodepool max to allow CA to add replacement nodes, but that has cost implications. What's the immediate plan?
maria: short-term plan I'm proposing:
1) cordon affected nodes and drain best-effort fast-fail GPU pods to CPU fallbacks where possible.
2) restart driver install job via machine image hook (we have a prebuilt script to reinstall kernel modules) on affected nodes.
3) if reinstall fails, reprovision new nodes from nodepool (bump max size) and retire broken ones.
Is everyone ok with that approach?
kenji: +1. For step 1, don't delete pods that hold state—use `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` and check for pod disruption budgets. Also, add a short dev loop: `kubectl logs -n kube-system ds/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset -l kubernetes.io/hostname=gpu-pool-7x9k` to watch.
raj: I'll prepare the driver reinstall command we use in the image build: `curl -sS https://internal-bins/driver-installer.sh | sudo bash -s -- --force --kernel-compat` — it rebuilds DKMS modules.
sophia: note on CA behaviour: unready nodes with taints can block scheduling for some controllers; and CA will not remove nodes until they're NotReady for the configured grace period. We should ensure the `scaleDownUnneededTime` isn't set too aggressively given transient driver issues.
infra-oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1422 - GPU nodes NotReady in us-west2. Pager sent to oncall.
cloudops: temporary action: I'm going to bump gpu-pool max from 5->8 to let CA add replacement nodes, will monitor cost. will revert after incident.
maria: performed cordon and started the reinstall script on gpu-pool-7x9k; I'll follow-up with logs.
(maria posts 12m later): reinstall looked successful on gpu-pool-7x9k, `lsmod | grep nvidia` now shows modules and `nvidia-smi` returns GPUs. kubelet transitions to Ready, device-plugin registers, taint removed automatically.
kenji: great. For long-term: we need to avoid kernel/driver drift during maintenance windows. Suggestments:
- pin a tested kernel-driver combo in our node image pipeline
- add a post-kernel-upgrade smoke test that runs `nvidia-smi` and reports back before marking node pool healthy
- create a pre-flight that prevents kernel updates on GPU nodes without validation, or schedule driver rebuild as part of the update flow
sophia: I'll open a follow-up ticket in infra backlog for the smoke test + image pinning. Also add CA nodepool max config review to ensure we have headroom for hot replacements; otherwise cost spikes are expected.
raj: I'll open a GH issue against our `infra-images` repo and include the DKMS reinstall step. also will open a bug against the nvidia-device-plugin repo to notify vendor if we see similar crashloops across kernel patch rollouts.
maria: thanks everyone — marking this thread resolved for now, will update INC-2026-1422 when everything's green. :white_check_mark:
cloudops: reminder to record the cost delta from the temporary nodepool bump and tag the incident for cost review.
sophia: noted — putting postmortem task on the calendar.
